A 49 year old male with
history of recently diagnosed panic attacks and recurrent rhabdomyolysis presents after a panic
attack at home leading to cardiac arrest with return of spontaneous circulation. Labs were
significant for an elevated potassium to 9.1 mmol/L and creatinine kinase of up to 220,000 U/L.
The patient was intubated for airway protection and admitted to intensive care unit (ICU) for
further treatment. While in the ICU, patient underwent hypothermia protocol for preservation of
neurological function and continuous renal replacement therapy for rhabdomyolysis. Further
medical history was obtained from the family that was notable for the history of developing a
shooting pain and muscle spasms in his left leg 1.5 years ago that caused him to have difficulty
walking, leading him to fall down a flight of stairs and causing injury in his thoracic spine that
required surgical stabilization. After the surgery, family noted the patient to have hour long panic
attacks with muscle stiffness and spasms throughout his body, particularly in his core muscles.
The patient had seen a multitude of neurologists and was provided negative lab results and
imaging, without a specific diagnosis. Given the abnormal quality of the patient’s presentation, an
anti-GAD 65 was sent that returned elevated. The patient was diagnosed with Stiff Person
Syndrome and subsequently treated with diazepam.
